'''paiN Gaming''' is a Brazilian esports organization.
== History ==
===Season 3===
In early 2013, paiN released their support [[MiT]] and top [[Tittu]], acquiring [[Espeon]] and [[Venon]]. The team then won [[Riot Season 3 Brazilian Championship]], which granted them a spot at the [[Gamescom 2013/International Wildcard Tournament|Riot Season 3 Int. Wildcard Tournament]]. They went 3-1 in the group stage, winning their game against [[GamingGear.eu]], but lost in the finals to the CIS team, who attended the [[Season 3 World Championship]] instead of them.
 
===2014 Season===
After losing at the IWC 2013, paiN decided to part ways with Espeon and pick up [[Minerva]]. With that roster, they placed second at [[IEM Season VIII - Sao Paulo]]. Then, [[brTT]] left to play for [[Keyd Stars]] and paiN fell into a rough patch, until they picked up Koreans [[Lactea]] and [[Olleh]]. With the two Korean bot laners, they won [[X5 Mega Arena 2|XMA - International Challenge 2014]] and [[Razer Challenge Brasil/Season 2|Razer Challenge Brasil Season 2]], but fell short to Keyd Stars and to [[CNB e-Sports Club]] at [[Riot Brazilian Champion League 2014]] and the [[2014 Season Brazil Regional Finals]], respectively.
 
===2015 Preseason===
After winning the [[IEM Season IX - San Jose/Qualifiers|Brazilian Qualifier]] (which also qualified them to the [[CBLOL/2015 Season/Split 1|CBLOL]]), paiN Gaming qualified as the Brazilian team for [[IEM Season IX - San Jose|IEM San Jose]]. They attended with a roster consisting of [[Leko]], [[SirT]], [[Kami (Gabriel Bohm Santos)|Kami]], Lactea, and Olleh and were eliminated in the quarterfinals, losing to [[Cloud9]] 0-2 and tying for fifth place in the tournament with [[Lyon Gaming (2013 Latin American Team)|Lyon Gaming]].
 
===2015 Season===
paiN had to release their Korean bot lane due to visa problems, and instead brought brTT and [[Dioud]] to the team. The team didn't click at first, placing fourth in the first split's [[CBLOL/2015 Season/Split 1|regular season]] and then third in the [[CBLOL/2015 Season/Split 1 Playoffs|playoffs]]. After they released Leko for [[Mylon]], everyone had high hopes for the team, and despite a shaky start, they won the [[CBLOL/2015 Season/Split 2|second split]]'s [[CBLOL/2015 Season/Split 2 Playoffs|playoffs]], defeating [[INTZ Red]], Keyd Stars and [[INTZ e-Sports|INTZ Team]], with Kami in particular standing out as a carry of the team. They qualified for the [[2015 International Wildcard Tournament/Chile|IWCT Qualifier]], and without dropping a single game the entire tournament qualified for the [[2015 Season World Championship]]. Analyst [[rnglol]]'s contributions to the team's success were particularly noted.<ref>[https://twitter.com/brttOficial/status/640275634426638337 brTT's tweet] ''twitter.com''</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KPdwjmv6jR0&feature=youtu.be&t=3h23m52s <nowiki>[PT-BR] KLG x paiN - Final do Desafio Internacional</nowiki> (Portuguese) (timestamped)] ''youtube.com''</ref><ref>[http://las.leagueoflegends.com/es/news/esports/esports-editorial/el-doloroso-camino-hacia-el-mundial-de-pain-gaming El doloroso camino hacia el mundial de paiN Gaming (Spanish)] ''las.leagueoflegends.com''</ref>

At Worlds, paiN were seeded into Group A along with [[Flash Wolves]], [[KOO Tigers]], and [[Counter Logic Gaming]]. They picked up two wins in the group, against eventual group winners Flash Wolves in the first week and then against CLG in the second week, and their 2-4 overall record and 1-1 head-to-head with CLG left them tied for third place, not advancing from groups. Despite their immediate elimination, paiN's group stage run was seen as a major success: they were the first Wildcard team to win more than one game at a World Championship and also the first Wildcard team to finish higher than sole possession of last place in their group. Additionally, they looked good in some of their losses: their second game against Flash Wolves lasted 52 minutes and could have gone either way at multiple points.

===2016 - 2019===
After the great success of 2015, paiN Gaming started to struggle over the years with multiple roster changes happening as key players such as their support [[Dioud]] left before the start of the 2016 season, [[brTT]] leaving after a dissapointing 6th place finish in the [[CBLOL 2016 Split 1|Summer]] and the team having to defend their spot during the [[CBLOL 2016 Split 2 Promotion|promotion tournament]]. During the two splits in 2017 the team managed to make it to the playoffs both times. However, they were not able to secure first place. Ahead of the [[CBLOL 2018 Split 1|summer season of 2018]], [[TinOwns]] became the new mid laner as [[Kami (Gabriel Bohm Santos)|Kami]] moved to an inactive position, and [[Takeshi]] became the new top laner as [[Mylon]] retired. These changes affected the team heavily as they finished in last place and the team ended up being relegated to the [[BRCC 2018 Split 2|BRCC]].

After the relegation paiN Gaming decided to rebuild their roster only keeping [[TinOwns]] and [[Matsukaze]]. The new roster contained [[Ayel]], [[Nappon]], [[TinOwns]], [[Matsukaze]], and [[Dioud]], who rejoined the team. This new roster finished 1st in the [[BRCC 2018 Split 2|group stage]], tied with [[Operation Kino]] and [[Team oNe eSports]]. As the team advanced easily to the finals after beating [[Team oNe eSports]] by 3-0 in the semifinals they fell short against [[Redemption eSports Porto Alegre|Redemption Porto Alegre]] as they got swept by a 3-0 and thus not directly promoting but moving to the [[CBLOL 2019 Split 1 Promotion|2019 promotion tournament]]. During the promotion tournament they faced their rivals, [[INTZ|INTZ eSports]], and once again paiN Gaming got swept for a 3-0, failing to promote back to the CBLOL. Once again the team decided on two changes: [[Minerva]] rejoined the team as the new jungler and [[esA]] joined from [[Flamengo eSports]] as the support. During the [[BRCC 2019 Split 1|Summer season of BRCC 2019]] they showed why they belonged in the CBLOL as they went 13-2, tied with [[RED Canids]] for first place in the group stage, and advanced to the playoffs once again. However, this time they swept [[Falkol]] 3-0 in the semifinals and [[Team oNe eSports]] in the finals, earning their spot back into the CBLOL and finishing their [[CBLOL 2019 Split 2|returning split]] with a fifth place finish.

== Trivia ==
* They were the first Latin American organization to have a gaming house.
* The team is often referred as the most traditional esports team in Brazil.
* The first Brazilian organization to reach the Worlds Main Stage since the end of the IWCQ in 2017, achieved during [[Worlds 2024]].
* Elected the Best Esports Organization in the '''Prêmio Esports Brazil 2024'''.
